context: mixed sports-civil & building programme · pitches, halls and accommodation run as parallel fronts

brief.intro: A sports academy or training facility is really several different projects running side by side: outdoor pitches with their sub-base and drainage, one or more indoor halls (and sometimes a pool), and standard accommodation/admin buildings for athletes and staff. Unlike a single building, there is no one chain that owns the whole site — pitch construction, indoor-hall structure and MEP, and accommodation fit-out can all run in parallel once each area's civil works are ready, so the programme is really a coordination exercise between several independent, medium-complexity work-fronts rather than one long sequence. The two things that most often surprise a first-time planner are how long pitch sub-base, drainage and grow-in take before a pitch can be certified for play, and how much the pool and specialist gym plant behave like a small industrial commissioning job inside an otherwise ordinary building.

must_get_right: Start pitch sub-base and drainage early and protect the grow-in period — natural turf needs real weeks to establish before certification, and that clock cannot be compressed by adding labour.

Treat pitches, indoor halls and accommodation as parallel work-fronts, not one sequence — plan and resource them separately, sharing only site-wide enabling works and access, so a delay on one does not need to delay the others.

Pool and specialist gym plant need their own small commissioning sequence — water treatment, filtration and heating plant behave like industrial equipment and need proving and balancing before use, not just installation.
Decide natural vs synthetic turf early — it changes both the construction sequence and the programme risk (grow-in weather-dependency vs a more predictable install-and-certify timeline).

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structural work runs a 6-day week; pitch grow-in follows a calendar period, not a working-day duration, and is weather- and season-dependent (turf establishment is slower in cold or wet periods); indoor MEP and pool commissioning run standard single-shift working.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Pitch sub-base, drainage, turf and grow-in typically form the longest single chain and often govern overall completion where natural turf is chosen; indoor-hall structure, MEP and pool/gym fit-out run as parallel fronts that only need to finish before their own building's handover. Where synthetic turf is used, the pitch chain shortens and the critical path can shift to pool/gym commissioning or accommodation fit-out instead.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Pitch type (natural vs synthetic) and specification are decided before sub-base construction starts; design for halls, pool and accommodation is frozen ahead of each front's start; each work-front (pitches, halls, accommodation) has its own dedicated crew so none compete for the same resource; weather allowances are built into the pitch and external-works calendars.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Pitch construction needs continuous, unobstructed access for sub-base and turf-laying plant and is highly weather-sensitive; the pool and gym fit-out need a clean, secure area late in the programme; specialist resources (turf contractor, pool-plant commissioning engineers) are shared across few crews and should be booked against a fixed window, not left open-ended.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: turf grow-in extension in poor weather/season, pool/gym plant commissioning slippage, and interface clashes where parallel fronts share site access or utilities. Contingency is held at the end of the pitch grow-in period and before pool/gym commissioning rather than spread across the parallel building fronts.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
